title: Guide to eyesight testing for NSW driver and rider licences
summary: This guide explains the requirements and procedures for eyesight testing for NSW driver and rider licences.

Individuals upgrading a licence to a higher class
Drivers and riders renewing or replacing a licence
Drivers and riders who are 45 years or older
Drivers and riders who are 75 years or older
Drivers and riders who have specific medical conditions or roles (e.g., heavy vehicle drivers, passenger transport service drivers)

faqs.q: When do I need to pass an eyesight test?
faqs.a: You must pass an eyesight test when applying for a driver or rider licence for the first time, when upgrading a licence to a higher class, or at specific intervals based on your age and circumstances.

faqs.q: How often do I need eyesight tests based on my age?
faqs.a: The frequency varies: every 10 years if under 45, every 5 years if over 45, and every year from age 75. You also need one if you haven't passed a test in the 12 months before renewing or replacing a licence, or when applying for a 10-year licence.

faqs.q: What happens if I have vision issues or need special conditions on my licence?
faqs.a: The guide covers conditions such as vision in one eye only (monocular vision), Glaucoma, and Macular degeneration, and details specific licence conditions (S001, S002, S003) that may apply.
